name: Question 19
problem:
Consider the vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where both $2\times 2$ blocks of $B$ represent rotation-scaling matrices:

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-7-6\text{i} \\ 4+4\text{i} \\ -2+5\text{i} \\ -1-2\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}-2+5\text{i} \\ -2-\text{i} \\ -3 \\ -1-7\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-4 & -3 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & -4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=-4-3\text{i}$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=2\text{i},$ respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$
worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a $4\times 4$ real matrix that has complex eigenvalues 

$\,$ ${\lambda }_{1}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{2}\,$ and $\,{\lambda }_{3}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{4}$ 

with corresponding eigenvectors 

$\,$ ${v}_{1}={\overset{―}{v}}_{2}\,$ and $\,{v}_{3}={\overset{―}{v}}_{4},$ 

then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 & 0 \\ -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{3}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{3}) \\ 0 & 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{3}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{3})\end{aligned}]
$$

and

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ \text{Re}({v}_{1}) & \text{Im}({v}_{1}) & \text{Re}({v}_{3}) & \text{Im}({v}_{3}) \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-4 & -3 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & -4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the first and second columns of $P$ correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and the third and forth columns of $P$ correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{3}.$ Therefore,

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}-7 & -6 & -2 & 5 \\ 4 & 4 & -2 & -1 \\ -2 & 5 & -3 & 0 \\ -1 & -2 & -1 & -7\end{aligned}].
$$

Consider the vectors v1 and v3 and the block diagonal matrix B shown below, where both 2×2 blocks of B represent rotation-scaling matrices: v1=[−7−6i4+4i−2+5i−1−2i],v3=[−2+5i−2−i−3−1−7i],B=[−4−3003−400000200−20] The vectors v1 and v3 are the eigenvectors of a matrix A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1=−4−3i and λ3=2i, respectively. Given that A=PBP−1, which of the following could be the matrix P?

a
[44−1−2−250−3−7−65−2−1−2−7−1]
b
[44−2−1−7−6−25−1−2−1−7−25−30]
c
[−7−6−2544−2−1−25−30−1−2−1−7]
d
[−6−7−2544−2−15−2−30−2−1−1−7]
e
[44−2−1−25−30−7−6−25−1−2−1−7]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Recall that if A is a 4×4 real matrix that has complex eigenvalues

λ1=λ―2 and λ3=λ―4

with corresponding eigenvectors

v1=v―2 and v3=v―4,

then A=PBP−1, where B=[Re(λ1)Im(λ1)00−Im(λ1)Re(λ1)0000Re(λ3)Im(λ3)00−Im(λ3)Re(λ3)] and P=[||||Re(v1)Im(v1)Re(v3)Im(v3)||||]. Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of B will result in switching the corresponding columns in P.

From our block diagonal matrix B=[−4−3003−400000200−20], we deduce that the first and second columns of P correspond to the complex eigenvector v1, and the third and forth columns of P correspond to the complex eigenvector v3. Therefore, P=[−7−6−2544−2−1−25−30−1−2−1−7].
